universal_lens: A canonical ledger operator induces a partial order on corrective actions, where each phase is a monotone map on the state space of artifacts. Dependency probes act as feasibility oracles that prune the execution DAG before resource commitment. Regression gates enforce a closure property: readiness equals passing all historical counterexamples.
gsi_mapping: The ledger functions as a conformal predictor's calibration set: each audit correction is a nonconformity score that updates the prediction interval for future script reliability. Phase ordering implements a Bayesian sequential design where early cheap probes (E.8) update the prior on expensive null-run budgets (T7).
gse_mapping: The executor embodies a situational reasoning agent with a fixed policy: read ledger → probe constraints → commit errata → gate regressions. State transitions are triggered by hard blockers (missing files) or feasibility verdicts. The two-pass audit architecture creates a dual-control loop: auditor proposes, executor disposes, theorist speculates.

primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P_k: phase k (dimensionless); E_j: execution item j (dimensionless); C: cost budget (CPU-hours); ≺_exec: execution partial order (dimensionless)

primitives.name: Dependency Feasibility Probe
primitives.verbatim_quote: If infeasible, recommend T7 be killed or rescoped before anyone spends its 400-null-run budget.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: I: import set (dimensionless); F: target filtration (dimensionless); Ω: allowed imports {nflreadpy, sklearn, numpy, pandas}; β: feasibility boolean (dimensionless); B: null-run budget (CPU-hours)
primitives.assumptions: Feasibility is decidable by cold import test; budget B is sunk only if β=1; kill/rescope decision is binary and irreversible.
primitives.breakdown_regime: False negative probe (β=0 but feasible with workaround); false positive (β=1 but runtime > budget); transitive dependency drift.

layer2.mapping: Probe ≡ conformal feasibility test; allowed imports ≡ hypothesis class constraint; 400-null-run budget ≡ prediction interval width; kill decision ≡ reject null of feasibility at α=0.05.
layer2.telemetry: Import test pass/fail; probe runtime; budget saved/killed.

primitives.name: Regression Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: A script is not "ready" until it executes cold end-to-end in your environment.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: R: regression ledger (dimensionless); D_i: defect i (dimensionless); A_i: assertion i (boolean); S: script submission (dimensionless); ready: readiness predicate (boolean)
primitives.assumptions: Defects are finitely enumerable; each defect maps to a decidable assertion; readiness is conjunction of all assertions; ledger is append-only.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Undecidable assertions; new defect class not covered by existing assertions; assertion flakiness (non-deterministic pass/fail).

layer2.mapping: Regression ledger ≡ conformal prediction's calibration errors; each assertion ≡ nonconformity measure; readiness ≡ prediction interval coverage guarantee; cold end-to-end execution ≡ out-of-sample validation.
layer2.telemetry: Assertion pass rate; time to pass all assertions; new defects per submission.

The canonical ledger operator establishes a supremum in the lattice of fix lists, inducing a monotone update on the artifact state space. The phased execution queue implements a cost-aware partial order where cheap probes (E.8) act as feasibility oracles before committing expensive budgets (T7's 400 null runs). This is mathematically a sequential decision process: the import probe computes a binary feasibility predicate β under import constraints Ω; if β=0, the value of information of the probe exceeds the expected cost of T7, triggering kill/rescope. The regression gate enforces a closure property: readiness(S) ≡ ∧_i A_i(S), where each assertion A_i encodes a historical defect D_i. This is isomorphic to conformal prediction where the regression ledger is the calibration set, assertions are nonconformity scores, and readiness is the coverage guarantee. The cold end-to-end execution requirement (quote 11) corresponds to out-of-sample validation. The two-pass audit architecture creates a dual control loop: Motif (architect/auditor) proposes corrections, DeepSeek (theorist) provides SPEC numbers, and the executor measures and commits. The errata protocol (quote 12) — corrections as addenda, originals untouched — preserves the audit trail as an immutable ledger, enabling retrospective conformal calibration.

reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Three agents with asymmetric capabilities: Motif (architect/auditor) sees the full ledger and proposes fixes but cannot execute; DeepSeek (theorist) generates SPEC numbers without an execution environment, so its outputs are unverified hypotheses; Executor (Claude) has the only execution environment, must measure to verify, and holds veto power via hard blockers (quote 8). The executor's incentives align with minimizing wasted compute (kill T7 early) and maximizing audit trail integrity (errata protocol). Motif's adversarial audit role means it will stress-test the executor's gates.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity: The import probe (E.8) and regression gate (E.11) must not share failure modes — probe tests dependency feasibility, gate tests logical correctness. Leakage veto: DeepSeek's SPEC numbers must never enter the regression ledger as assertions; only measured defects from executor runs qualify. Budget veto: If probe runtime > 1% of T7 budget, the probe itself becomes a cost risk. Immutability veto: Any direct edit to original files (bypassing errata/addenda) invalidates the ledger's supersession order and breaks conformal calibration.
